addendum9.clause: ADDENDUM 9 §9.1: the per-lane reading governs the frontier; both readings are computed, sealed and printed for every child
addendum9.derivation: the charged lanes are already counted as observed misses in the useful-or-partial total, so the per-lane reading re-scores nothing; it decides only whether the degeneracy clause fires, which it does when the degeneracy is general and does not when it is confined to identifiable lanes

axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 1.0000 on the sealed corpus and 0.0992 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it
axes.selection: the 10240 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 4633 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt
